summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with a history of systolic heart failure (EF 15%), atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and alcohol abuse, was admitted with chest pain and dizziness after reporting multiple episodes of AICD firing, which was later ruled out. He had a significant drop in hematocrit from baseline to 26.6%, prompting concern for internal bleeding due to a recent altercation involving abdominal and head trauma. CT scans of the head and abdomen showed no acute hemorrhage. He was transfused one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia, with improvement in hemoglobin to 10.8 g/dL by discharge. Chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, not cardiac or infectious, and resolved with acetaminophen. Pradaxa was held initially but restarted at discharge due to high thrombotic risk. Alcohol withdrawal was managed supportively, and the patient declined referral to a treatment program. He was discharged home in stable condition with clear instructions to avoid alcohol and seek immediate care after any fall or trauma.
problems: Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
